fact: Minister of Digital Transition said negotiations with Starlink are advancing and the state hopes soon to decide whether to let it offer services to the population, so no authorisation has yet been given.

ARCEP found Starlink supplying satellite internet by selling terminals in Burkina Faso without the authorisation the 2008 law requires, and stated Starlink held no authorisation to offer electronic communications services there.

Starlink's availability map lists Burkina Faso as 'Starting in 2026' with coverage or regulatory authorisation pending and no launch date; the service is not yet available there, though it had been shown for 2025.

Le360 lists Burkina Faso among markets shown by Starlink as available from 2026 with no licence granted; ARCEP recalled in March 2024 that Starlink held no authorisation, and unofficial use via roaming is reported.
MyBroadband's status table lists Burkina Faso with estimated Starlink availability '2026', not 'Available', so no service was on sale.
Semafor reports Starlink had been blocked from approval in seven countries including Burkina Faso; no event date given, so the article date is used.
The Ministry of Digital Transition lists finalising Starlink's entry into the Burkinabe market as a 2026 priority, so Starlink was not yet in the market at the 23 March 2026 meeting.
